results.market_title: Coca-Cola (KO) Q3 organic revenue (non-GAAP) growth 6.5% to 8%?
results.reasoning: Coca-Cola's own FY2026 guidance of ~5% organic revenue growth, following Q1 (+10%) and Q2 (+6%) results, implies the H2 2026 (Q3+Q4) revenue-weighted average must fall to roughly 2% to hit the full-year target, even before accounting for a flagged structural headwind of six fewer selling days in Q4. Q3 2026 faces a tough prior-year comp (Q3 2025 was already a strong +6%), and management's commentary points to a clear deceleration narrative rather than acceleration into the 6.5-8% band. While some of the H2 slowdown could be concentrated more in Q4 (due to the day-count headwind), allowing Q3 to land somewhat higher (plausibly 4-6%), reaching the 6.5-8% bracket would require Q3 to buck the deceleration trend Coca-Cola itself has guided toward.

results.reasoning: NJ-01 is a safe Democratic seat (Cook PVI roughly D+10, Harris won it by ~19 points in 2024) held by longtime incumbent Donald Norcross, who has won recent general elections by wide margins (historical data points to roughly 17-27+ point victories in 2022 and 2024). xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator).

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1); exit fees and the US spread are not charged on those. marks.x5 / marks.x15 are the round trip: closed on the Polymarket US book 5 / 15 minutes later (the bid for a buy, the ask for a sell, so the spread is paid) with the exit taker fee charged too - what a scalping lane would actually have booked. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, a Polymarket US lane is worth building only if the round trip (x5 or x15) is positive on the tradable subset with a hit rate above 50%, or settle is; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.
